obligations.condition: A fresh pending credential completes the phone second factor at the start of the run; identity confirmed by claims and a derived lookup. Establishes that the machinery works before any aging.

A pending credential held untouched for about 2 seconds is presented to mfaSignIn:start with a freshly opened SMS session. Accepted or refused are both valid observations; no TTL is pinned. The pending age and the session age are recorded separately.
If the 2-second start returned a session, that fresh session is finalized; skipped otherwise. Token checks are recorded as booleans, not required.
A pending credential held untouched for about 120 seconds is presented to mfaSignIn:start with a freshly opened SMS session. Accepted or refused are both valid observations.
If the 120-second start returned a session, that fresh session is finalized; skipped otherwise.
A pending credential held untouched for about 300 seconds is presented to mfaSignIn:start with a freshly opened SMS session. Accepted or refused are both valid observations.
If the 300-second start returned a session, that fresh session is finalized; skipped otherwise.

A fresh pending credential completes the phone second factor after all aging; confirms the flow still works at the end, so a refused aged row reflects the pending age and not a broken run or exhausted quota.

limitations: Revision 1 samples only 2, 120 and 300 seconds; every sampled age is below the 3600-second fireemu-local pending lifetime, so a fully-usable run establishes a lower bound on the lifetime, never an infinite lifetime or an exact TTL.

The corpus does not separate which of the pending credential or the SMS session expires first, and does not test an expired pending combined with an independently valid code; those are later corpora once feasibility is established.
No claim about tenants, blocking functions, SDKs, Security Rules, or the exact error precedence.
